correctness.rationale: The asserted graph GP(8,3) has exactly 16 vertices, 24 simple edges, and degree three. A recursive first-unmatched-vertex matching enumerator produces 33 perfect matchings and 20 unordered three-factor partitions; independent direct backtracking of all proper edge colors after exact S3 normalization reproduces the same full 20-state set. Two logically distinct quotient adjacency methods, connected alternating-cycle flips and pairwise single-cycle symmetric difference, agree on the entire graph. A stated explicit bijection checks all 120 candidate pairs of distinct large-component vertices and certifies edge AND nonedge equivalence with the 24-edge original graph. A full 120-state named-coloring expansion and breadth-first search from all vertices verifies component orders 24/96, edges 54/288, degree distributions and exact radii, diameters and ordered distance spectra. The exhaustive enumerations prove only this finite graph; no infinite-generalization claim is made.

value.rationale: Edge-Kempe switches are the natural elementary reconfiguration operations on 1-factorizations of cubic bipartite graphs at their chromatic index. Showing that one full component of this classical symmetric graph’s *own* quotient switch graph is isomorphic to the original graph is a mathematically motivated self-copy phenomenon, not just a count, renaming or arbitrary parameter. The disjoint four-star gives contrasting local geometry; the labeled 24/96-state distance census separates component equivalence from transition cost. These structural data are not determined by known two-class counts and provide a concrete finite benchmark for factorization reconfiguration.
